newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks edge down at open after Dow fall.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks edge down at open after Dow fall.

text.p: Australian shares opened slightly weaker on Thursday as investors factored in a 34 point fall from the Dow and a weaker gold price.
At 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 2.8 points at 2,430.7.

Stocks opened narrowly mixed with bellwether issue BHP continuing to drift lower, while major banks opened slightly firmer. National Australia Bank edged higher after it announced stronger first quarter results.

"The Dow was only down last night because of the IBM situation where as the S&P 500 was up nicely. Our market is being influenced by metal prices with gold down again last night so it should finish off but only by about five or six points," said Peter Struk, a dealer at Sydney brokerage, Reynolds and Co.
Struk said the market had seen a small amount of profit-taking over the past few sessions and was seeing more of the same this morning.
Industrial issues were outperforming resources due to the resilience of the bank sector while resources were weighed down by selling in major mining issues CRA and WMC.
At 10.45 a.m. (2345 GMT), CRA shares were 24 cents weaker at A$19.26 (US$14.83), while WMC shares were two cents weaker at A$8.23.
